Series::gelu¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::gelu() const -> Series
Series::gelu(bool approximate) const -> Series
Series& Series::gelu_() const

What It Does¶

gelu() applies the Gaussian Error Linear Unit activation elementwise:

gelu(x) = x * Phi(x)

where Phi is the standard-normal cumulative distribution function. Instead of the hard on/off gate of relu(), each input is scaled by the probability that a standard-normal draw falls below it — so a large positive x passes through almost unchanged, x = 0 maps to 0, and negative x is softly suppressed with a small dip below zero.

Phi(x) has no elementary form, so there are two evaluations:

  • gelu() and gelu(true) use the fast tanh approximation x * 0.5 * (1 + tanh(sqrt(2/pi) * (x + 0.044715 * x^3))).

  • gelu(false) uses the exact form built on erf(), x * 0.5 * (1 + erf(x / sqrt(2))).

The two agree to about three decimal places everywhere.

gelu() needs a floating-point input (it is built on tanh / erf).

Parameters¶

approximate (bool, optional)

true (the default) selects the tanh approximation; false selects the exact erf-based form.

Returns¶

Series or Series& The activated values, same shape and floating-point dtype as the input.

Gradient¶

gelu() is differentiable. Its derivative is

d/dx gelu(x) = Phi(x) + x * phi(x)

where phi is the normal density. It equals 0.5 at x = 0, rises above 1 for moderate positive x (the x * phi(x) bump), and tends to 1 for large positive x and 0 for large negative x. Unlike relu(), the gradient is smooth and nonzero for small negative inputs, so gelu() units do not “die”.

In-Place Form¶

gelu_() is the in-place sibling of gelu(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — gelu_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-1.0, 0.0, 1.0});
x.gelu_();
std::cout << x;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.15865525, 0, 0.84134475]

Examples¶

Example 1. The soft gate: near-identity on the right, a small negative dip on the left.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0}).gelu());

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.0036, -0.1588, 0.0000, 0.8412, 2.9964]

Example 2. The exact erf-based form differs only in the last digits.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0}).gelu(false));

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.0040, -0.1587, 0.0000, 0.8413, 2.9960]

Example 3. The backward is Phi(x) + x * phi(x) — 0.5 at the origin and above 1 for moderate positive x.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.gelu().sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.0116, -0.0830, 0.5000, 1.0830, 1.0116]

The negative entries at x = -3 and x = -1 are the smooth non-zero gradient that keeps the unit trainable where relu() would give exactly 0.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The default is the tanh approximation. Pass gelu(false) if you need the exact CDF form.

  • Floating-point input only; an integer series raises (the error names the internal tanh).

  • The gradient can slightly exceed 1 for moderate positive x; that is the x * phi(x) term, not a bug.

Summary¶

gelu(x) is x * Phi(x) — a smooth, probabilistic gate:

  • gelu() / gelu(true) use the tanh approximation; gelu(false) the exact erf form

  • floating-point input only

  • differentiable, smooth and nonzero for small negatives, so units do not die

See Also¶

  • Series::silu: x * sigmoid(x), the closely related smooth gate.

  • Series::relu: the hard-gate baseline gelu() softens.

  • Series::erf: the primitive behind the exact form.
